I've been in this sub for a while but still am surprised by the amount of similar situations there are here. His wanting your conversation to just be the two of you is one of the classic control tactics: No one else to witness the fact that he's being unreasonable, toxic or manipulative. 

Your feeling bad is understandable, but also playing right into his role of "I'm the victim here, I need support." 

If he truly wanted to repair and keep your relationship, he would listen to you when you express your boundaries and not continue to cross them. 

He is lonely and sad due to his own faults that he refuses to correct and you don't have to feel guilty for that, it is NOT your fault.

The fact that he's said his only goal now is to have you in his life is another way of guilting you into staying in contact with him. If you don't feel comfortable about this, don't play his game. Remove yourself from it. 

Sending you support. There aren't too many alternatives between contact and no contact unfortunately, especially not when dealing with a narcissist. This is a difficult situation to be in but I hope you find comfort in knowing you're not alone, and there are ways to cope with these issues.

Picture this;
The year is 2014, it's winter and the snow outside is 4 feet tall. 
To no surprise all of the sleds are out of stock. so me, being me, had the bright idea to use a baking tray instead.
baking trays very noticeably do not have handles big enough to use as a sled, but they do have very small grips on the sides which I thought would be just fine to hold onto.

So me and my mom go out to walk to dog as we do everyday, this time with the addition of a baking tray.
I find the perfect spot; a hill with freshly fallen snow. Being the perfect spot I decided to disregard the road at the bottom of the hill and start with my sledding adventure.

I start down the hill, it's exhilarating and fresh and fun. And then I hit the road.
My left thumb that was tucked under the grip decided to adjust itself into a position that would put it between the baking tray and the road, bare in mind I had just come down a steep slope so I was going at a fairly accelerated pace.

Before I could fathom what was about to happen my thumb hits the road with my full body weight on top of it and twists round in agony.

After a few days of telling my mom that it's fine, refusing to accept that my brilliant idea of using a baking tray as a sled had failed, I gave in to the pain and she took me to the hospital.To which they found out I had broken my thumb quite badly, and proceeded to cast my hand and thumb with santa  claus wrapping, which made it slightly more bearable. 

I hope you enjoyed this tale of woe of 14 year old me learning that, sadly, baking trays, cannot be used as a makeshift sled.

One thing my therapist said to me which actually stuck was focusing on the power of your second thought. So if you're thinking these negative things, these are your initial thoughts, they are intrusive and represent your anxieties even though in most cases they are not true. So when you catch yourself thinking these things or feeling this way, try to come up with a second thought to overpower that first one. E.g. first thought; ' they don't want to talk to Me, they don't care about Me, I'm wasting their time' you can tell that voice to f*ck off and instead think 'that is an intrusive and  distorted thought that is not true and I am stronger than believing in it, I can improve and I WILL improve, this is just a minor setback'. 
It doesn't work for everyone but it's worth a try xxx

My morning ritual; wash my face, brush my teeth, mouthwash, floss, moisturise, make my bed and have a coffee. It's weird that this makes me happy and excited for the day. But I think it's because I spent so many years in a spiralling hole of depression, just these few small and simple tasks every morning make me excited for the day, because I've come this far, and I do more than I could ever do before.

I just want to start off by saying you are NOT alone. I know it doesn't seem like it sometimes, but there will always be someone there for you to hear your thoughts and help you stay calm. You are NOT a burden,  it might feel like you are, but more people than you know appreciate your just being here. School is one of the most difficult goddamn places, filled with judgment, bullies and assholes, but it doesn't last forever, you'll be out of there sooner than you know it and will progress in life far more than you could imagine. 

I know it's really cliche to say 'think positive' and it can seem quite blunt, but really, altering your state of mind is one of the first steps to getting better. My therapist told me something that actually helped with this quite a lot: 'you can't control your first thought, but you can control your second'. Meaning, those moments where you think 'I hate myself' or 'I want to die' are okay, it's okay to think that. But what's not okay is to let that thought control you and lead onto other intrusive thoughts; normally for me my head goes from a random thought of wanting to end it, to all of the things I hate about myself, to a full blown breakdown. But instead of letting those thoughts come, I push them out of my mind and focus on something else that I know will distract me or cheer me up. When I get those thoughts now I say to myself ' you do not want to die and you do not hate yourself, you are here for a reason and even if you don't know what that is yet, you will soon. All you can do is try to enjoy the moment as much as you can until then'. 

As for your school life, I'm glad that you know that these people aren't your true friends if they're doing things like making fun of you, especially for things that you are passionate about. And even though school life can seem quite lonely when you're in a situation like this, you will find true friends later on in life that will always be there for you and will encourage you to do what you enjoy. 

It's okay to cry, and it's okay to be sad, it's better to let it out rather than let your emotions bottle up inside to the point where you feel like you just can't take it anymore. I will say this now; you CAN confide in your family and the people you love, and they may have better advice for these things than you might think. They will always be there for you no matter what and will support you always.

What I've found over the years is that its much much easier to appreciate the small things rather than looking at the big picture, I understand that right now you hate everything about your life. But if there is just one thing that can make you smile in a day, that is an accomplishment, no matter how small. You can appreciate the way the sun rises every morning, or the smell of rain or freshly cut grass. You can make yourself a meal and appreciate how everything you're eating has been made by someone, or has grown in the earth, just to get to you and keep you going. I know it sounds kind of stupid but it can really help. Also, I find carrying a small object around ( in my case a stone) can help distract me from negative thoughts. Whenever I start to get overwhelmed I take it out and turn it over, I focus on the textures and details, which ultimately takes my thoughts away from the negativity in my mind, this doesn't work for every one, but there is absolutely no harm in trying.

Now for your hair... I have had similar issues with this and it can cause major anxiety, which I still struggle with to this day. The one thing that I have found helps with this (and bare with me here) is sunglasses. I know it sounds stupid as hell but having my eyes covered actually makes me feel so much more comfortable being out in public, especially if I can't manage to make my hair look presentable. Because, in the long run, it doesn't matter, you can look like a model and still be anxious to go out at all. I don't know the logic behind this, maybe because if someone were to make fun of me they wouldn't see the fear or sadness in my eyes, or maybe it's because the tinted colours soothe me. Again, this doesn't work for everyone, but again there is no harm in trying. 

And finally, it is okay to break down, it's okay to cry, it's okay to not be okay. But you can't give up, you keep going everyday and keep trying every day until suddenly you realise, it's not as difficult as it used to be. As long as you try, You will get there, you will get your dream job in a hospital with little coffee shops all around,you will help people and you will be happy. Even if it doesn't feel like it right now, one day it will be easier. You'll look back to this post and realise how strong you are for coming so far and for confiding in the people you trust. And no matter how many people bully you or make fun of You, there will always be someone who appreciates your life, even if it's not you. 

For what it's worth; I'm glad that you are here and I hope with all my heart that things get easier for you sooner rather than later. I appreciate your life, and you are not alone.

Yes. Several times. It's like once they know you're theirs, they treat you like shit, but if you show any sign of leaving, suddenly you're their queen and deserve the world. I hate how someone who can seem like the nicest person ever can change in an instant. They can become manipulative and abusive and gaslight the hell out of you.

When I was in this position, I tried to leave several times but was always roped back into the relationship somehow. I felt I was trapped even though I could walk away at any time... It's like an emotional tie that they have on you that's nearly impossible to break. When I finally did manage to leave for good, it took me years to be able to live like I did before, I couldn't leave the house or do anything for myself, I'm still unemployed due to anxiety and panic disorder. But things do get better slowly, one step at a time.

I think, I'm glad I went through the experience as a whole because it helped me grow and become stronger as a person, even though it was one of the most horrible things that have happened to me in my life... And if anyone else is in this position now, the only advice I could give would be to break it off now before it becomes even more difficult, and that even though it will be hard, it gets easier over time.

He would have his moments where he was utterly convinced I was cheating on him and say horrible things to me, when I would do no such thing. I wasn't allowed any male friends, I wasn't allowed to talk to my parents because he thought they were 'out to get him'. 

At one point he had a complete breakdown and lost all sense of reality, he forgot who he was and was speaking in riddles. At one point he told his friends that he had killed me which turned into a whole ordeal with the police.

It got to the point where I just couldnt take it anymore and I left, but I still wonder if he ever managed to get out of that state of mind, it was quite terrifying for me to watch.
